findings.title: Denial cache returns stale deny without DB revalidation
findings.body: In Service.Check the denial-cache hit at lines 116-121 returns Allowed:false immediately without re-querying permissions. If a permission is granted after a denial was cached (e.g. dashboard/folder just created and ACL added, role grant, share), the user stays denied for shortCacheTTL (30s). This re-introduces the exact staleness the PR claims to fix and turns a transient deny into a pinned deny.

findings.title: Folder tree still cached with no fallback, new folders invisible
findings.body: Service.Check now refreshes permission scopes from DB on cached-permission miss, but checkInheritedPermissions/buildFolderTree still serves folderCacheKey unconditionally for shortCacheTTL. A newly created folder (or dashboard parent linkage) is not in the cached tree, so inherited folder:uid checks fail even after fresh permissions are loaded, the request is denied and then a denial entry is cached. List has the same problem via listPermission->buildFolderTree.

findings.title: Denial cache key can collide on underscores
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds namespace+".perm_"+userUID+"_"+action+"_"+name+"_"+parent with plain underscore joins. Names, UIDs and actions can contain underscores, so (name=a_b, parent=c) and (name=a, parent=b_c) produce the same key. A denial cached for one resource can then incorrectly deny a different resource.

findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type
findings.body: The denial key is namespaced by namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent but not by IdentityType. The same UID string can exist for different types (user vs service-account, anonymous:0 vs user id 0). A denial recorded for one identity type can short-circuit Check for a different identity type with the same UID string.
